title: Swimming hall — entrance
prompt:
Create one high-fidelity visual mockup of an immersive personal portfolio website for Storm Selvig. This is the entire first-person web experience, 1536x1024 landscape, flat screen capture, no browser/device frame. There is no hero layout, tagline, title section, cards, branded colour scheme, navigation bar, or marketing copy. The whole viewport is a coherent explorable 3D environment. Only a tiny unobtrusive plain white 'Storm Selvig' at the top left and small 'Index' and 'Sound off' controls at the bottom right overlay the scene.

The fictional environment is an old modest northern-European indoor swimming hall gradually converted into a personal workspace. It must feel curious, specific, quiet, slightly odd and inhabited, not luxury architecture, not a futuristic laboratory, not a colorful toy scene. The swimming pool is EMPTY AND DRY. Viewpoint is at ordinary human eye level on the shallow-end walkway looking diagonally across the whole rectangular pool and at the far wall; use realistic 24mm architectural perspective, not fisheye or isometric. Strong coherent spatial layout: left foreground broad tiled steps descend into the dry pool, whose floor is only 1.4m lower; a plain plywood worktable with a running ordinary monitor, keyboard, scattered papers, headphones and task lamp sits on the dry pool floor toward the far left; at the far deep end an unframed project screen is projected softly onto a white tiled wall, with a stool and an old unobtrusive projector aimed at it. On the right side, three open changing-room doorways along the surrounding walkway lead into small side spaces, one lit with a desk visible, one holding shelves and handwritten notes. A normal visible stair at far right leads to a narrow upper gallery above those same changing rooms, with railing, a row of windows and some pinned photographs. The walkway fully loops around the pool and connects all these areas. Several paths are visibly available at once; there is no stage sequence.

Materials determine the colours: aged pale grey grout, imperfect off-white small square tiles with old faded green ceramic strips at the original water line, dull stainless pool ladders and rails, worn pale timber doors, ordinary darker plywood furniture, broad high frosted windows with soft overcast daylight. Mild wear, repaired tiles, old drain, realistically messy cables arranged near worktable, paper taped by one doorway; sparse human details, not staged decor and no plants everywhere. There is one abandoned yellow foam swim board leaning by a ladder as a small optional interactive object. Ceiling trusses and tall windows give depth, use subtle atmospheric distance but keep the entire room clear and readable. Natural shadows, uneven ordinary materials, convincing geometry, beautiful yet understated real-time-render style. No neon, no pastel set, no orange/cobalt accent objects, no chrome spheres, no glowing lines, no giant floating 3D project models. All contents are normal scale.

Near the descending steps, a small white circle and understated hovered label 'Pool floor' indicate a clickable destination. The other route entrances use only tiny white dots. A discreet bottom-left hint reads 'Choose a place to move'. A small genuine screen on the table may show project thumbnails but avoid invented legible project claims. No numbered steps or arrows imposing a route. This must read as the starting view of an actual explorable browser environment, with quiet useful UI and absolutely no promotional language. Composition has no reserved blank copy area. Scene occupies every edge. Show architectural spatial coherence and clear walkable routes, not a generic concept painting.
notes: Fictional environment. Still mockup, not a working 3D implementation.
